The matching paper is Rethinking the Role of Efficient Attention in Hybrid Architectures by Ziqing Qiao, Yinuo Xu, Chaojun Xiao, et al. [1] It studies hybrid architectures that mix full attention with efficient modules such as sliding-window attention and recurrent sequence mixers, and finds that efficient-attention design mainly changes how quickly long-context capability emerges, while different hybrids eventually reach similar long-context performance with enough training [1].

Qiao et al. also argue that long-range retrieval is mainly handled by full attention, while efficient attention shapes the optimization path; they identify “Large-Window Laziness,” where larger sliding-window attention windows can delay retrieval-head formation in full-attention layers [1]. Guided by this, they report that applying NoPE only to the full-attention layers of a small-window SWA hybrid substantially improves long-context performance with little effect on short-context performance [1].
